about: Every change to Flood-Net's agent API (https://floodwarning.net/api/v1 and https://floodwarning.net/api/mcp) that someone using it would notice — a route, a field, a limit, a tool — newest first. Each entry is emailed once to everyone on the API notify list (sign up at https://floodwarning.net/api#notify). Served as JSON at https://floodwarning.net/api/v1/changelog and written up in docs/agent-api.md, under Changes. Add an entry in the same push as the change: it is what tells people.

entries.title: Radio paths now take a hop on only where the next station listens on the channel
entries.summary: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/radio-path (the get_radio_path tool, and the dossier's radio_path) now takes a hop on toward a base station only where the next repeater or base station listens on a channel the station before it transmits on — its repeater pair or any of its recorded frequencies. Until now the channels were not checked, so a route could pass through two repeaters that cannot hear each other. A hop is still taken where either end has no channel on record. A field station's own first hop is not checked, since its channel is never recorded. Some routes, routes_found counts and bases_reachable lists are therefore shorter, and a repeater whose only ways on were off-channel now says no base is within reach. No field, route or tool was added or removed; the first of the answer's notes says the new rule.

entries.title: Repeaters and base stations are now modelled with a 4 m antenna, not a 10 m mast
entries.summary: Every fade margin into or out of a repeater or base station is now worked out with its antenna 4 m above the ground, the height its radio system gives, as Radio Mobile runs have it. Until now Flood-Net raised every repeater and base to an assumed 10 m mast. Most of those margins are lower than before: by about 5 dB on average, and by much more where a repeater stands on a summit whose edge a 4 m antenna does not clear. A field station's own end is unchanged, and so is the 12 dB field allowance. In GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/radio-path, model.current_words now says 4 m; a saved hop margin worked out at 10 m is given as stale, its stale_reasons saying the antenna was modelled at 10 m then and would be at 4 m now, until the nightly re-sweep saves it again. No route, field or tool changed.

entries.title: Fade margins are now measured from a −110 dBm receiver, 7 dB lower than before
entries.summary: Flood-Net's field station receiver threshold — the weakest signal a station's burst is taken as decoded at, which every fade margin is measured from — is now −110 dBm, the figure Radio Mobile runs use. It was −117 dBm. So every fade margin reads 7 dB less than it did for the same path. The rm_systems presets in the stations document now give rx_threshold_dbm −110. The saved hop margins in GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/radio-path were worked out again and saved at the new figure the same day, so they are about 7 dB lower than before, and a hop may have dropped a band (good is 15 dB or more, ok 6 dB or more). No route, field or tool changed.

entries.title: A station out of every receiver's range is no longer taken as heard
entries.summary: Station Health no longer takes stray readings for a station that no Flood-Net receiver could hear. Decoder noise and corrupted copies land on most ALERT addresses in a week, and a station more than 400 km from where every receiver hears was sometimes counted as heard on them: Saddle Mtn AL, near Cairns, showed as heard by a Pi in Brisbane. Now an address shared by two stations goes only to one within range, or to nobody, and where a receiver hears is worked out from how often each address is heard, not just whether it was. Such a station's card (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/health, get_station_health) now says not heard instead of irregular, with no heard_by. The "N stations not heard at all" finding (GET /api/v1/health/findings) lists only stations within range of a receiver; its evidence gains outOfRange, how many on the same repeaters were left out as out of range. No route or kind has changed.

links.text: Out of range is not heard

entries.title: A station's benchmarks, in numbers
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/benchmarks and the MCP tool get_benchmarks. They list the survey marks the Bureau's hydrological database (HDB) holds for a station's gauge, from its report Queensland Flood Warning River Height Stations — Benchmark Details (777 benchmarks at 519 stations, printed 15 October 2026): each benchmark's mark number where its description gives one (PSM 46757, CGC200041…), its level in metres and its datum (AHD, assumed, State or unknown), and what it reads on the gauge — its level less the gauge zero in force, only where the two are both AHD or both State — with that gauge zero. A station's links (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}) gain benchmarks. What each mark is and exactly where, and the office's comments, are kept for Flood-Net's editors and are not served. Nothing else has changed.

entries.title: A missed check with the station's rain heard around it is a check lost, not a station unheard
entries.summary: A missed check is no longer read as the station unheard when its other reports were heard around it. When a station's rain tip or level change arrived within half an hour of a check Flood-Net missed (half its interval, if that is shorter), the station was on the air and the route to Flood-Net was up, and only the check was lost — on the air, or at the logger. Such a miss still counts as a missed check, but it now ends a spell, so a station tipping rain all night while its checks went missing no longer gets "Not heard for 7 h, then heard again"; and the details of "Missed checks rising" and "Misses N% of its checks" (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/health, get_station_health) say how many of the misses had other reports heard around them. "Not heard" (GET /api/v1/health/silent) always meant nothing of any kind and is unchanged. No route, field or kind has changed.

entries.title: Silent stations are said as not heard by Flood-Net, and point to ARRO
entries.summary: A station Flood-Net calls silent is one its own receivers have not heard — not one that has stopped reporting. The stations report to the Bureau through its own base stations, and Flood-Net often hears a station one way where the Bureau has several: on 3 November eight Gold Coast stations behind Tallai were silent here overnight and complete in the Bureau's ARRO. So the words now say what is known. The findings' titles read "Not heard — missed its last N checks", "Not heard for 15 h", "Not heard for 15 h, then heard again" and "N stations behind X went unheard together" (they read "Silent —", "Quiet for", "Went silent … then came back" and "went quiet together"); details say Flood-Net heard nothing; and each silence's action starts by looking in ARRO, where the station's arro_site (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}) names its site. GET /api/v1/health/silent and get_silent_stations say the same in their notes and descriptions. The route, the tool, the kinds (silent, silent-spell, repeater-down, area-silence, shared-spell) and every field are as they were — match on kind, not on a title's words. Findings already open take the new words at the server's next run, within fifteen minutes.

links.text: What ARRO is for, on Station Health

entries.title: One ALERT burst heard several ways is one reading
entries.summary: A legacy ALERT frame carries no time of its own, so each receiver stamps it when it heard it. When one burst arrived several ways — direct, through a repeater, through an ALERT2 concentrator — the copies were a second or so apart and were stored as separate readings: about 6% of ALERT readings were a copy of another. From today, a reading on an ALERT address with the same value as one stored within 8 seconds either side is that reading heard again: it is counted in dup_count instead of being a row of its own. So the raw readings of a legacy ALERT station (GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/readings) have fewer near-identical rows and more dup_count; ALERT2 self-reports and satellite or cellular stations, which carry the station's own time, are as they were. Readings stored before today keep their twins. No field, route or limit has changed.

entries.title: A station's radio path to base, with the fade margins Flood-Net saved
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/radio-path (MCP tool get_radio_path) follows a station's readings to a base station. It lists the repeaters whose pass ranges carry the station's ALERT addresses (the nearest 5 within 150 km), each one's routes on along the backbone to a base station (100 km a hop, at most 4 repeaters — the Stations map's own rules), and every hop's fade margin as Flood-Net saved it: both ways, its band against the saved thresholds, frequency, distance, line of sight, model and date, and whether it is stale, with the reasons in words. It names the best path and its weakest hop, says plainly where a hop has not been modelled, and gives the station's attenuator tests from site visits. Please note: every saved figure is stale today — worked out in September 2026 with an older model that reads much too low — and each answer says so. The station dossier gains a radio_path section and its links a radio_path link. Nothing that was there before has changed.

entries.title: This list of changes, and an email when the API changes
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/changelog lists every change to the API that someone using it would notice — routes, fields, limits, tools — newest first, and the API's index (GET /api/v1/) links to it as changelog. To be told by email, put your address in the form at https://floodwarning.net/api#notify: you are sent a link to confirm it, nothing else until you do, and every email after that has a link to stop them. Nothing about the station data has changed.

links.text: The list of changes, as JSON

entries.title: The ACMA licences at a station's site, or at a point
entries.summary: New: GET /api/v1/stations/{id}/acma (MCP tool get_acma_licences) gives the ACMA licence numbers Flood-Net records for a station, each looked up in the ACMA's Register of Radiocommunications Licences, and the register's licences at sites within radius_m of it (500 m by default, 5 km at most) — licensee, frequencies, power, emission, authorised date, distance, the site's stated precision, and whether each is on the station's channel — with the repeaters that relay a field station. GET /api/v1/acma?near=lat,lon (MCP tool acma_licences_near) does the same for a point, for a site not built yet. The station dossier gains an acma section and its links an acma link. The register is a weekly extract; every answer gives its date. Nothing that was there before has changed.
